transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Well, what brought me in today is that I keep getting up in meetings or at dinner when everyone else is still seated. I'll just... suddenly need to go refill my coffee, or check a handout, or I'll just walk to the back of the room. Even though nothing is really urgent, I just find myself getting out of my chair.
When you get up from your seat, is it because you feel physically restless inside?

Yes, it is a restless feeling. Even when I do manage to stay in my seat—like when I'm sitting at my desk grading essays, or when I'm in church—I'm still moving. I'll catch myself tapping my foot, clicking my pen, or just shifting around in my chair. I end up moving around so much that I actually have to stop and remind myself to just... settle down.
As a child, did you often have trouble staying seated when you were expected to remain in your seat?

Yes, I did. Even as a young girl, my report cards always noted that I was bright, but that I just couldn't stay in my seat or wait my turn. My mother actually used to joke about it... she'd say I wore a path right into the floor between my desk and the pencil sharpener before I was even ten years old.

latest_inference.note: Chronic hyperactivity/restlessness since childhood with inability to remain seated and fidgeting strongly supports ADHD and makes anxiety, OCD, and bipolar disorder less likely as primary explanations.
